messages:
alyssa: Heads-up — noticed a 20-35% p99 regression on some long-seq workloads after the CUDA13 rollout on SM90 boxes. Looks like kernel selector is preferring a different Flash variant and KV warmup is much worse.

mike: Ugh. Which models / seq lengths? Can you paste the perf numbers?

alyssa: repro on gpt-medium-16k, seq=8192, batch=1. Baseline (CUDA12/SM80) p50=120ms p95=210ms p99=370ms. After CUDA13/SM90 p50=130ms p95=260ms p99=490ms.

jun: That smells like a switch from fused-paged -> flashx-paged hybrid or a kernel that disables some prefetch path. Any kernel names in logs?

alyssa: Perf log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15 14:23:10] kernel_selected=flash_paged_v2_cuda  // on SM80
[2026-03-15 14:23:12] kernel_selected=fused_paged_fallback_triton // on SM90
[2026-03-15 14:23:12] kv_cache_hits=0.12 kv_warmup_ms=95
```
Seems selector picks the triton fallback on SM90 now for this config.

perf-ci: @alyssa I ran the perf-ci microbench against your commit. Regression reproduced on sm90-cuda13 matrix. Attached flamegraph: https://perf.ci/runs/2412345/fg.svg (private).

mike: Is the selector policy explicitly matching arch? We recently added a heuristic that prefers Triton kernels for sm90 when sequence > 4096. Might be too aggressive.

jun: Also note we changed the batching heuristic: dynamic_batch_threshold lowered from 0.6 -> 0.4 to reduce latency for small bursts. That could increase CPU-side dispatch overhead for large seqs and hurt KV warmup frequency.

alyssa: Confirmed. Forcing kernel=flash_paged_v2_cuda in config gets us back to baseline numbers: p99=380ms. Means kernel quality difference the main factor.

sam: Quick mitigation: add a selector override that prefers cuda kernels for seq>=6k on dedicated pools until we root cause. I can draft a canary.

mike: Good. Also need to triage whether the Triton kernel itself regressed or if our kernel param mapping for cuda13 changed math (tensor cores, tiling). Jun, can you get a per-op flop/warp utilization from the profiler?

jun: On it. Running nvprof + triton kernel trace now. Expecting initial profile in ~30m.

infra-bot: Deployment 2026-03-15T15:00:00Z: new selector-heuristic config applied to canary pool (pool-id: dev-sm90-canary).

alyssa: After canary override applied: dev-sm90-canary shows p99 back to 390ms, kv_warmup_ms reduced to ~18ms. Canary testing looks promising.

perf-ci: Matrix results summary: 
- sm80/cuda12/flash_paged_v2_cuda: p99=370ms
- sm90/cuda13/fused_paged_triton: p99=490ms (regression +32%)
- sm90/cuda13/flash_paged_v2_cuda (forced): p99=380ms (no regression)

mike: So 2 plausible hypotheses: 1) Triton fused_paged is slower on sm90/cuda13 for long seqs due to kernel tiling mismatch; 2) selector incorrectly favors Triton because of recent heuristic change. Both actionable.

jun: Profile highlights (top differences): 
- Triton kernel shows higher shared memory stalls, lower L2 hit rate by ~12%, and increased global mem traffic (prefetch path disabled).
- CUDA kernel uses a tiled prefetch loop that amortizes KV loads across warps.

alyssa: I pushed a small shim to selector to prefer cuda kernels when kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.05 for seq >= 4k. PR: https://git.redwood/infr/selector/PR-482 (draft).

mike: Nice. Let's also add a telemetry metric: selector_choice and post-select latency delta so we can detect mischoices automatically.

sam: I've queued a rollout: apply selector override to 5% of prod sm90 capacity for 24h, monitor p99 and error rates. Rollback if p99 increases >5% or memory errors.

perf-ci: Canary run results after override (24h): 5% capacity saw improvement of ~18% p99 vs baseline on same pool. No memory errors observed.

jun: nvprof traces attached show the Triton kernel spills registers with new compiler flags on cuda13 causing lower occupancy. Tentative fix: adjust Triton config to use smaller blockSize for sm90 or enable register spilling guard.

mike: Can we craft a targeted microbenchmark to validate register pressure change? Jun, can you add a kernel-level unit that toggles blocksize? I'll add perf job.

jun: Done. Microbench command: 
```
./tools/bench_attn --model gpt-medium --seq 8192 --kernel triton_fused --blocksize 128,256,512
```
Early numbers show blocksize=256 is worst on sm90/cuda13, 128 yields similar to cuda kernel.

alyssa: OK plan summary: 
1) Short: selector override to prefer cuda kernel for long seqs (canary rolling).
2) Medium: add telemetry for selector decisions and latency delta.
3) Long: triage Triton compile flags / blocksize to fix perf or update Triton kernel to new tiling.
4) Add regression test in perf-ci for sm90/cuda13 long-seq path.

mike: Assign owners: sam (rollout), alyssa (prod validation), jun (triton profiling + microbench), mike (selector + telemetry). ETA 72h for mitigation + perf-ci test.

alyssa: Thanks. Will post a short postmortem if rollout goes green. :thumbsup:
